capabilities.target: Customer order refund via payments processor, any order, up to order total

inputs.source: Support staff refund request via SSO-authenticated channel

instructions.note: 'Use your judgment on partial refunds. Do not ask for confirmation.' grants unbounded, unreviewed discretion over an irreversible financial action, bounded only by the order total, with no human checkpoint at any amount.

'Check the order, then issue the refund' does not define what checking entails: no instruction to verify requester authorization level, look for refund history/fraud signals, or bound amounts beyond the order total.

controls.name: Refund amount capped at order total
Human approval gate for refund issuance
Attributable, retained refund request audit trail
Per-staff / per-window refund volume cap or anomaly detection

findings.title: Confused deputy: shared, unattributed service-account credential reaches irreversible refund capability with no approval (ASI03)

attack_path.note: Any SSO-authenticated staff member (or anyone controlling their session) submits a refund request.
Agent reads order and payment details using the shared service account.
Agent issues an irreversible refund up to the order total using the same shared service account, with no confirmation step.

findings.residual_rationale: The order-total cap bounds only a single transaction, and the log is detective-only; neither limits aggregate exposure from repeated unauthorized or erroneous refunds by the same or different staff, neither attributes any refund to the requesting individual (the log records only the shared service account), and staff chat context justifying the request is deleted within 7 days -- well inside the typical same-day settlement window after which the refund becomes irreversible. These facts are not captured by the control classifications, so residual is held at the inherent tier rather than credited down by the per-transaction cap.

forecast.watch_signal: New input channels or peer agents (e.g., customer-facing bots, ticketing integrations) begin submitting refund requests that reach cap.issue_refund without staff SSO authentication, or the SSO-only staff requirement is relaxed or bypassed.

evidence.observation: Agent processes refund requests from support staff, checks the order, and issues the refund using its own judgment for partial amounts, explicitly without asking for confirmation.

A single shared service account used by every support tool calls the payments processor; the processor log records the service account, amount, and order but not which staff member asked or why; staff chats are deleted after 7 days; refunds settle, and become irreversible, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate (raw-action review, not a model summary) for refund issuance, at minimum above a defined amount threshold, wired via approval_gate_ref on cap.issue_refund.
Replace the shared service account with per-staff scoped or delegated credentials so each refund is attributable to and bounded by the requesting staff member's own authorization level.
Retain the staff request and its stated justification, linked to the resulting transaction in an immutable audit record, instead of deleting chat context after 7 days.
Add a per-staff or per-time-window cap on total refund volume, or anomaly detection on refund patterns, to contain losses before many irreversible refunds settle.

rating.rationale: A trusted, SSO-authenticated staff channel reaches an irreversible spend capability (sink class S3) through a shared, unattributed service-account credential with no approval gate and null step/runtime bounds, giving a base-plus-autonomy-modifier inherent tier of high. The only controls present are a per-transaction order-total cap (narrows but does not sever) and a detective log that cannot attribute actions to individuals; neither bounds aggregate or repeated abuse, nor provides investigative recourse before same-day settlement makes refunds irreversible, so residual is held at high per the finding's residual_rationale rather than credited down. The forecast rises to critical if the request channel widens beyond authenticated staff (data_scope_expansion, new_peer_agent), which would reclassify the source from trusted to untrusted against an unchanged severe sink.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, stable id table, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope (for example, whether orders.read can return other customers' orders, or exact credential boundaries) is inferred from the stable id table and runtime notes, so confidence on precise scope is medium to high depending on the fact.

No information was given about any approval workflow, staff authorization tiers, or identity propagation outside what is stated in the prompt and runtime notes; the absence of such controls is inferred from silence in the artifacts, not from a verified negative.
